title: Valdivia culture
description: Villagers on the coast make some of the earliest pottery in the Americas.

title: Death of Huayna Capac
description: The Inca emperor dies in the north of his empire, probably of a disease brought by Europeans, and his sons Huáscar and Atahualpa fight over the succession.

title: Quito founded
description: Sebastián de Belalcázar founds the Spanish city on the ruins of the Inca town.

title: Guayaquil founded
description: Francisco de Orellana settles Guayaquil at its present site, later the country's main port.

title: Expedition to the Amazon
description: Gonzalo Pizarro leaves Quito to look for cinnamon, and his lieutenant Francisco de Orellana goes on to travel the length of the Amazon.

title: Audiencia of Quito
description: Philip II creates a high court at Quito whose district is the basis of the later country.

title: French Geodesic Mission
description: French and Spanish scientists arrive to measure a degree of latitude at the equator, work that later gives the country its name.

title: Quito Revolt
description: The people of Quito rise against new taxes and a royal liquor monopoly and drive out the Spanish officials for a time.

title: First junta of Quito
description: Creoles depose the president of the Audiencia and set up a governing junta, remembered as the first cry of independence.

title: Independence of Guayaquil
description: Guayaquil declares independence from Spain and becomes the base for the liberation of the highlands.

title: Battle of Pichincha
description: Antonio José de Sucre defeats the royalists on the slopes above Quito, ending Spanish rule in Ecuador.

title: Guayaquil Conference
description: Bolívar and San Martín meet in private, after which San Martín withdraws and leaves the liberation of Peru to Bolívar.

title: Separation from Gran Colombia
description: An assembly in Quito declares the southern district a separate state under Juan José Flores.

title: Darwin in the Galápagos
description: HMS Beagle reaches the islands, annexed by Ecuador three years before, where Darwin makes observations that later shape his theory of evolution.

title: Assassination of García Moreno
description: The conservative president Gabriel García Moreno, who had built a strongly Catholic state, is killed outside the government palace.

title: Liberal Revolution
description: Guayaquil proclaims Eloy Alfaro supreme chief, beginning the Liberal rule that separates church and state.

title: Guayaquil–Quito railway completed
description: The first train from the coast reaches Quito, linking the two halves of the country.

title: Killing of Eloy Alfaro
description: A mob drags the former president and his companions from prison, kills them and burns their bodies.

title: Guayaquil general strike
description: Troops fire on striking workers, killing hundreds, in the founding event of the Ecuadorian labour movement.

title: Rio Protocol
description: After its defeat by Peru, Ecuador signs a treaty giving up its claim to a large part of the Amazon basin.

title: Oil found at Lago Agrio
description: A Texaco and Gulf consortium strikes oil in the Amazon lowlands, which makes Ecuador an oil exporter from 1972.

title: Return to democracy
description: Jaime Roldós takes office as elected president, ending seven years of military rule.

title: Indigenous uprising
description: The indigenous federation CONAIE blocks roads across the highlands, making indigenous peoples a force in national politics.

title: Peace with Peru
description: Ecuador and Peru sign an agreement fixing their border, three years after the Cenepa War.

title: Mahuad overthrown
description: Indigenous protesters and army officers remove President Jamil Mahuad days after he adopts the United States dollar as the currency during a banking collapse.

title: Correa elected
description: Rafael Correa wins the presidency after a decade in which three presidents were forced from office.

title: Constitution of 2008
description: Voters approve a constitution written at Montecristi, the first in the world to give rights to nature.

title: Earthquake of 2016
description: An earthquake on the northern coast kills more than 600 people.

title: Protests of 2019
description: Protests led by indigenous groups force President Lenín Moreno to restore fuel subsidies.
